subject: Math
title: Geometry & mensuration
sub: Angles and polygons, circle theorems, similarity and symmetry, area, surface area and volume
strategyIntro: Extended Maths is two papers of equal weight: Paper 2 (2 hours, 100 marks, no calculator) and Paper 4 (2 hours, 100 marks, calculator). Your school test may be shorter, but it is marked the same way: M marks for a correct method, A marks for the correct answer that follows, B marks for a correct result on its own.

strategy.title: Timing
points: About 1.2 minutes per mark: a 5-mark question is worth about 6 minutes.
If a question has taken twice its time, leave a gap and come back at the end.
Keep 10 minutes at the end to check answers against the question.

strategy.title: Show your working
points: Most marks are method marks. A wrong answer with clear working can still score most of the marks.
Write the calculation you are doing before the answer, e.g. 360 ÷ 12 = 30.
An answer with no working can score zero if it is wrong, and sometimes even if it is right ("show that").

strategy.title: Paper 2: no calculator
points: Practise fractions, negative numbers, standard form and surds by hand.
Leave answers exact when you can: fractions, surds, or in terms of π.
Check with a quick estimate: is the answer about the right size?

strategy.title: Paper 4: calculator
points: Give answers to 3 significant figures unless the question says otherwise; angles to 1 decimal place.
Never round partway through. Keep the full value in the calculator memory (or write 4+ figures).
Use the π button, not 3.14. Check the calculator is in degrees.

strategy.title: Answer the question
points: Read the last line again: units, form of answer ("in its simplest form", "in terms of π"), and accuracy.
"Show that" questions: every step must be written, ending with the given result.
When the question says "hence", use the previous part.

commandWords: Calculate
Work out from given facts. Show the working; usually a calculator is allowed.
Work out / Find
Get the answer by any correct method. Show working.
Write down
The answer needs little or no working: you can often read or state it.
Show that
The answer is given. Write every step clearly so the examiner can follow the logic to it.
Estimate
Round each number (usually to 1 significant figure) and calculate a rough value.
Simplify
Write in its simplest form: collect like terms, cancel common factors.
Factorise (completely)
Write as a product of factors. Completely means take out every common factor.
Expand
Multiply out the brackets.
Solve
Find the value(s) of the unknown that make the equation or inequality true.
Sketch
Show the shape and key features (intercepts, turning points), not plotted accurately.
Describe fully
For a transformation: name it and give every detail (centre, angle, direction, scale factor, vector or mirror line).
Hence
Use the result you have just found to answer this part.
Give your answer in its simplest form
Cancel fractions and ratios fully; simplify surds.
quizIntro: Quick calculations and concept checks. Do each one on paper first, then pick. The wrong options are common mistakes, so if you got one, read the working in the explanation.
flashIntro: Methods, rules and formulas. Say the rule out loud (or write it down) with an example before you tap, then check you remembered every step.

flashcards.back: Angles on a straight line add to 180°; angles around a point add to 360°; vertically opposite angles are equal.
Alternate angles are equal; corresponding angles are equal; co-interior angles add up to 180°.

flashcards.front: Angle sums of triangles and quadrilaterals
flashcards.back: Triangle: 180°. Quadrilateral: 360°.

flashcards.front: Sum of interior angles of an n-sided polygon
flashcards.back: (n − 2) × 180°. Pentagon: 540°; hexagon: 720°.

flashcards.front: Exterior and interior angle of a regular polygon
flashcards.back: Exterior = 360° ÷ n. Interior = 180° − exterior.

flashcards.front: Finding the number of sides from an exterior angle
flashcards.back: n = 360 ÷ exterior angle. Exterior 24° → 15 sides.
Equals the sum of the two interior angles opposite it.

Parallelogram: opposite sides equal and parallel, opposite angles equal. Rhombus: also all sides equal, diagonals cross at 90°. Kite: one pair of equal angles, diagonals at 90°. Trapezium: one pair of parallel sides.
Name the fact in words each time: "alternate angles are equal", "angles in a triangle sum to 180°". "Z angles" may not score.
The angle at the circumference subtended by a diameter is 90°.
A tangent meets the radius at the point of contact at 90°.

flashcards.front: Two tangents from an external point
flashcards.back: They are equal in length. With the two radii they form a kite, symmetrical about the line to the centre.
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference subtended by the same arc.
Angles at the circumference subtended by the same chord (on the same side) are equal.
All four vertices on a circle. Opposite angles add up to 180°.
The angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment (the angle at the circumference on the other side of the chord).

flashcards.front: Perpendicular from the centre to a chord
flashcards.back: It bisects the chord (cuts it in half).
Use full words, e.g. "opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180°". Also look for isosceles triangles made by two radii.
Same shape, different size: corresponding angles are equal and corresponding sides are in the same ratio (the scale factor k).
If lengths are multiplied by k, areas are multiplied by k² and volumes by k³.

flashcards.front: Finding k from areas or volumes
flashcards.back: From an area ratio: k = √(area ratio). From a volume ratio: k = ∛(volume ratio). Then use k for lengths.
SSS, SAS, ASA (or AAS) and RHS. AAA only shows similarity.

flashcards.front: Similar triangles with a parallel line
flashcards.back: If DE is parallel to BC (D on AB, E on AC), triangles ADE and ABC are similar. Use the whole side AB, not just DB.
The order is the number of times the shape looks the same in one full turn. A regular pentagon has order 5.
A plane that cuts a 3D shape into two mirror-image halves. A cuboid with three different edge lengths has 3; a cube has 9.
Perpendicular bisector: points equidistant from two points. Angle bisector: points equidistant from two lines. Leave the compass arcs visible.
1 cm on the drawing represents 200 cm = 2 m in real life.
½ × base × perpendicular height (or ½ab sin C with two sides and the angle between them).
base × perpendicular height (not the slanted side).
½(a + b)h, where a and b are the parallel sides and h is the distance between them.
C = πd = 2πr.
A = πr². Use the radius, not the diameter.
Arc length + 2 radii. Forgetting the two straight edges is a common mistake.
1 m² = 100 × 100 = 10 000 cm²; 1 cm² = 100 mm². Square the length conversion.
Leave π as a symbol: radius 6 → area 36π. Do not use a calculator value.
Area of cross-section × length. Cylinder: πr²h.
Curved surface 2πrh; total (closed) 2πrh + 2πr².
⅓ × base area × perpendicular height.
Volume ⅓πr²h. Curved surface area πrl, where l is the slant height.
Volume (4/3)πr³. Surface area 4πr².
Volume (2/3)πr³. Curved surface 2πr²; with the flat circle, total 3πr².
l = √(r² + h²) by Pythagoras, where h is the perpendicular height.
1 litre = 1000 cm³. 1 m³ = 1 000 000 cm³ = 1000 litres.
Volume of the whole cone minus the small cone cut off. Use similar triangles to find the missing height.

quiz.q: What is the interior angle of a regular hexagon?
quiz.why: Exterior = 360 ÷ 6 = 60°, so interior = 180 − 60 = 120°. (60° is the exterior angle.)

quiz.q: A regular polygon has an exterior angle of 24°. How many sides does it have?
quiz.why: n = 360 ÷ 24 = 15. (156° is the interior angle.)

quiz.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of a decagon (10 sides)?
Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One co-interior angle is 65°. What is the other?
quiz.why: Co-interior angles add to 180°: 180 − 65 = 115°.

quiz.q: Which quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides?
quiz.why: A trapezium has one pair of parallel sides. Parallelograms and rhombuses have two pairs; a kite has none.

quiz.q: The angle at the centre of a circle is 130°. What is the angle at the circumference subtended by the same arc?
quiz.why: The angle at the circumference is half the angle at the centre: 130 ÷ 2 = 65°.

quiz.q: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral. Angle A = 78°. What is angle C?
quiz.why: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to 180°: 180 − 78 = 102°.

quiz.q: AB is a diameter and C is on the circle. Angle CAB = 35°. What is angle ABC?
quiz.why: Angle ACB = 90° (angle in a semicircle). 180 − 90 − 35 = 55°.

quiz.q: PT is a tangent at T to a circle with centre O. Angle TOP = 62°. What is angle OPT?
quiz.why: Angle OTP = 90° (tangent ⟂ radius). 180 − 90 − 62 = 28°.

quiz.q: The angle between a tangent and a chord is 48°. What is the angle in the alternate segment?
quiz.why: Alternate segment theorem: the two angles are equal, 48°.

quiz.q: Two similar triangles have corresponding sides 4 cm and 10 cm. The smaller has area 12 cm². What is the area of the larger?
quiz.why: k = 10/4 = 2.5, area factor 2.5² = 6.25. 12 × 6.25 = 75 cm². 30 cm² uses k instead of k².

quiz.q: Two similar bottles have heights 10 cm and 15 cm. The small one holds 400 ml. How much does the large one hold?
Two similar solids have surface areas 25 cm² and 64 cm². What is the ratio of their volumes?
quiz.why: Length ratio = √25 : √64 = 5 : 8. Volume ratio = 5³ : 8³ = 125 : 512.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a condition for congruent triangles?
quiz.why: Three equal angles only show the triangles are similar; they could be different sizes.

quiz.q: What is the order of rotational symmetry of a regular pentagon?
quiz.why: It looks the same 5 times in a full turn (every 72°).

quiz.q: What is the area of a circle of diameter 10 cm, in terms of π?
quiz.why: Radius = 5, so area = π × 5² = 25π. 100π uses the diameter as the radius.

quiz.q: Find the arc length of a sector with radius 9 cm and angle 80°.
quiz.why: 80/360 × 2π × 9 = 80/360 × 18π = 4π cm. 18π cm² is the sector AREA.

quiz.q: A trapezium has parallel sides 7 cm and 11 cm, and height 6 cm. What is its area?
Convert 3.5 m² to cm².
What is the perimeter of a semicircle of radius 5 cm?
quiz.why: Half the circumference = 5π = 15.71, plus the diameter 10: 25.7 cm. 15.7 cm forgets the straight edge; 39.3 is the area.

quiz.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 3 cm and height 10 cm, in terms of π.
quiz.why: π × 3² × 10 = 90π. 60π cm² is the curved surface area.

quiz.q: Find the volume of a sphere with radius 6 cm, in terms of π.
quiz.why: (4/3) × π × 216 = 288π. 144π is the surface area 4πr².

quiz.q: A cone has radius 5 cm and height 12 cm. What is its slant height?
quiz.why: l = √(5² + 12²) = √169 = 13 cm. (√119 subtracts instead of adds.)

quiz.q: How many cm³ are in 2.4 litres?
A cube has volume 64 cm³. What is its total surface area?
quiz.why: Edge = ∛64 = 4 cm. 6 faces × 16 = 96 cm².

examIntro: Paper 2 / Paper 4 style. [No calculator] questions are Paper 2; [Calculator] questions are Paper 4. Write full working first, then open the mark scheme: M1 = method mark, A1 = accuracy mark (correct answer from correct working), B1 = mark for a correct result on its own. Give yourself one mark per point you got.

exam.q: [No calculator] Find the size of one interior angle of a regular 12-sided polygon.
[No calculator] The angles of a pentagon are x°, (x + 20)°, 2x°, 100° and 120°. Find x and the largest angle.
[No calculator] Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 7 times its exterior angle. (a) Find the exterior angle. (b) Find the number of sides.
[No calculator] A, B and C are points on a circle with centre O. Angle AOC = 140° and B is on the major arc. Find angle ABC. Give a reason.
points: B1: the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference

exam.q: [No calculator] PA and PB are tangents from P to a circle with centre O. Angle APB = 40°. Find (a) angle AOB (b) angle OAB. Give reasons.
points: M1: OA = OB (radii), so triangle OAB is isosceles: (180 − 140) ÷ 2

exam.q: [No calculator] A, B, C and D lie on a circle in that order. AC is a diameter. Angle BAC = 32° and angle CAD = 25°. Find (a) angle ACB (b) angle BCD (c) angle BDC. Give a reason for each answer.
points: B1: angle ABC = 90° (angle in a semicircle)
A1: angle BCD = 180 − 57 = 123° (opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral)
B1: angles in the same segment are equal (BDC and BAC both stand on BC)

exam.q: [No calculator] Triangles ABC and PQR are similar, with AB corresponding to PQ and BC to QR. AB = 6 cm, BC = 9 cm and PQ = 8 cm. Find QR.

[No calculator] In triangle ABC, D is on AB and E is on AC, with DE parallel to BC. AD = 4 cm, DB = 6 cm and DE = 5 cm. (a) Find BC. (b) The area of triangle ADE is 8 cm². Find the area of the trapezium DBCE.

[Calculator] Two mathematically similar cones have volumes 135 cm³ and 320 cm³. The smaller cone has height 9 cm. (a) Find the height of the larger cone. (b) The curved surface area of the larger cone is 400 cm². Find the curved surface area of the smaller cone.
[No calculator] A sector has radius 6 cm and angle 120°. Find its area, giving your answer in terms of π.
[Calculator] A circle has area 200 cm². Find its circumference.
[Calculator] A garden is a rectangle 12 m by 8 m with a semicircle of diameter 8 m attached to one of the 8 m sides. Find (a) the area of the garden (b) the perimeter of the garden.
exam.note: The 8 m side joined to the semicircle is not part of the perimeter.

exam.q: [No calculator] Find the total surface area of a cuboid measuring 5 cm by 4 cm by 3 cm.
[Calculator] A cylinder of radius 4 cm holds exactly 1 litre of water when full. Find its height.
[Calculator] A solid is made from a hemisphere of radius 6 cm with a cone of radius 6 cm and height 8 cm on its flat face. Find (a) the volume of the solid (b) the total surface area of the solid.
exam.note: The flat faces are joined together, so they are not part of the surface area.
